display.title: Tu B'Shvat: What a Tree Teaches Us
display.summary_short: Tu B'Shvat is the New Year for trees: we eat fruits of Eretz Yisroel, say Shehecheyanu, and learn from a tree that our fruits are good deeds and our hands reach up to Hashem.
display.summary_long: A short Tu B'Shvat talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, broadcast on the eve of the day in 5748. Uncle Yossi explains that tonight is Rosh Hashanah for the trees, the fifteenth of Shevat. We celebrate by eating fruits, especially the seven species for which the Torah praises Eretz Yisroel, and a new fruit we have not tasted all year so we can say Shehecheyanu. The Sages teach that we can learn from a tree: its most important part is its fruit, and a person's most important fruits are good deeds, Torah and mitzvos. A tree's branches also reach upward, like a person raising his hands to pray to our Father in Heaven. When we tie ourselves to Hashem, we never fall. The talk introduces a story that is not included in this clip.
display.lesson: Like a tree, our real fruits are good deeds; reach upward to Hashem in prayer and stay tied to Him through Torah and mitzvos.
